newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 31.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Thanks largely to falling interest rates, which have benefited the entire listed property trust sector, General Property Trust has announced a total return to shareholders for 1996 of 13.6 per cent - almost double that of its main rival, Westfield Property Trust. GPT Management Ltd chief executive David Ross said yesterday the trust had at least A$300 million to spend on new property. Page 1.

Mobil Oil Australia announced yesterday it had applied to the Industrial Relations Court for an injunction to stop three unions - the Construction, Mining and Forestry Union, the Australian Manufacturing Workers Union and the Communications, Electrical an Plumbing Union - from taking industrial action in a long-running dispute on a troubled construction site at its Melbourne oil refinery. Page 5.

In a result described by Crown executive chairman Lloyd Williams as "very pleasing", the group has reported a 65 per cent rise in its interim earnings to A$30.1 million - the profit was struck on a nine percent increase in revenue to A$244.7 million, of which about 30 percent was attributed to high-rollers, mostly from South-East Asia. Page 39.

Due to drops in sales of life insurance business and a decline in investment earnings on its reserves, Norwich Union Financial Services' profit, reported under the life insurance industry's margin on services accounting rules, fell from A$52 million to A$7.4 million in the year to December 31. Page 39.

As speculation increased that Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation Ltd was looking at a A$1 billion purchase of New York's Madison Square Gardens, shares in News slumped yesterday, falling three per cent, or 20 cents, to A$6.48, while the preference shares sumped four per cent, or 21 cents, to A$5.30. Page 39.

IAMA Ltd chairman Nick Greiner told the national rural merchandiser's annual general meeting in Melbourne yesterday it had effectively given up its takeover battle for Queensland pastoral group Primac Holdings Ltd, indicating instead it would sit on a major shareholding. Page 41.
THE AUSTRALIAN

WMC Ltd is pushing to join the world resources stage as it currently negotiates to join an international mining consortium in an estimated A$6.3 billion joint venture to buy control of the world's largest iron ore miner, the Brazilian Government-owned Comanhia Vale do Rio Doce. Page 23

Southcorp Holdings Ltd managing director Graham Kraehe has joined the growing list of business leaders criticising the Federal Government over a lack of long-term national vision. Addressing a Committee for Economic Development of Australia meeting, Kraehe also said there was an urgent need for tax-reform. Page 23

Nine consortiums have made offers to the Federal Government for the Melbourne, Perth and Brisbane airports by the close of bidding yesterday. Details of the bids, estimated to raise between A$2 billion and A$3 billion, are not expected to be released until late February, with the successful bids announced before June 30. Page 23

In a report handed down by the Australian Broadcasting Authority, it has been proposed that the new digital television spectrum - set to form the basis of TV for the next 50 years - be allocated to the existing free-to-air broadcasters, rather than allocating new licences. The new technology will allow each broadcaster to transmit up to six channels instead of the existing one. Page 23

Rural groups remain divided over plans for the commercial restructuring of the Australian Wheat Board where a share-based corporate model has been proposed. The wheat industry now has under a month to reach a united front on the issue or face the prospectof having a resolution being imposed by the Howard Government. Page 25.

With less than four weeks until the scheduled court hearing between Optus Vision and Kerry Stokes' Seven Network Ltd, it is believed the three foreign shareholders of Optus Communications have opposed an out of court settlement with Seven, leaving Mayne Nickless, a 25 per cent shareholder in Optus, alone in its bid to push for a settlement. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Consortiums led by the Macquarie Bank and the Commonwealth Bank were firming yesterday as front-runners to take the Melbourne and Brisbane airports as part of the Federal Government's A$3 billion-plus airport auction. Nine separate parties lodged bids before yesterday's 4pm deadline. Page 25.

Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday showed new car registrations were down 0.1 per cent in December compared with the previous month and up 3.8 per cent through-the-year in seasonally adjusted terms. Meanwhile, newspaper job advertiements grew 2.1 per cent in January after falling for most of 1996. Page 25.

The A$10 billion partial privatisation of Telstra is gaining momentum, with the Federal Government inviting stockbrokers to pitch for roles in Australia's largest-ever float. Major broking houses County NatWest and SBC Warburg were excluded from bidding de to their business dealings with rival communications company Optus Communications. Page 25.

Office products group Ausdoc has reported a 26 per cent jump in net profit for the half year to June 30. Ausdoc's net profit before goodwill was A$3.56 million compared with A$2.84 million previously and the group struck a 13 per cent increase in sales to A$59.4 million. Page 25.

Shares in Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation fell sharply yesterday as rumours of a plan to buy New York's Madison Square Garden and associated sporting franchises reached the market. News' ordinary shares fell 20 cents to A$6.48 over market concern of how the purchase would be funded. Page 24

Melbourne's Crown Casino intends to lift its take of big-stake Asian gamblers by opening offices in Taipei and Beijing to attract more Chinese players. Crown yesterday announced December half-year profits of A$30.1 million from revenues totalling A$271.7 million. Page 27.
THE AGE

After yesterday reporting a December half-year net profit of A$30.1 million after abnormal costs of A$9.9 million from revenue of A$271.7 million, Crown Casino chairman Lloyd Williams said the Casino is conducting intense marketing in Asia and intends to ift its profit from big-stakes Asian gamblers by more than a third this half-year after opening offices in Taipei and Beijing. Page C1.

After losing an estimated A$20 million in additional advertising, lost sales and capital expenditure from a salmonella scare, Kraft chief executive officer Tom Park says the company's biggest peanut butter brand has reclaimed 40 per cent of the market, jut one month after the famous spread reappeared on supermarket shelves. Page C1.

United States chain West Coast Entertainment Corp yesterday acquired Melbourne-based rental chain Movieland, which has 108 stores nationwide, in a move which Movieland founder and managing director Tony Romano says will see Movieland able to expand and compete on a store-for-store basis with bigger groups such as Video Ezy and CIVIC video stores. Page C1.

As Optus Communications looks set to delay its stockmarket float until 1998, the A$10 billion partial privatisation of national telecommunications carrier Telstra is moving along rapidly, with the Howard Government yesterday sending letters to a handful of stockbrokers for the coveted roles of global coordinators and lead managers to the float. Page C1.

According to figures for the six months to December, Southgate, the sole asset of the Paladin Commercial Trust, achieved a net income of A$13,607,000 for the six months to December - A$1,048,000 above prospectus forecasts. Trust directors yesterday attribued the strong performance to higher income from the car-park complex on the banks of the Yarra River and cost savings across all components of the Melbourne complex. Page C3.

David Ross, the chief executive of General Property Trust, Australia's largest listed property trust, yesterday predicted the group would have about A$300 million available for acquisitions after announcing a 36.7 per cent increase in profit to A$167.7 milion for the year to December. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
